own_solution.law: tau - tau_f = I*alpha, I = (1/2) M R^2
assumptions: Disc rotates in the sense of the driving torque

T05A7.regime: disc already rotating (kinetic friction governs); also static friction < driving torque

T6122.regime: disc already rotating (kinetic friction governs); also static friction < driving torque

defect_reasons.other: The K regime 'static friction < driving torque' is not the operative reason: the problem says the disc already rotates, so kinetic friction governs regardless of the static value; the certified in-regime answers are still correct.

notes: Checked R answers: q=1 -> I=0.15625, alpha=28.8; q=2 -> I=0.1875, alpha=24; q=5.5 -> I=0.296875, alpha=15.158 rad/s^2; all correct. C cancellation via rho = m/(pi r^2 t) holds.
